chunks: Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Ibn Abi Umayr from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'A woman from our family is mixed up (insane/confused); is there Zakat upon her?' He said: 'If it was worked with (i.e., her wealth was utilized/managed), then Zakat is upon her, and if it was not worked with, then no.'
ai.seo_question: Is Zakat obligatory on the wealth of an insane person?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies that Zakat liability for the wealth of an insane person (majnun) is contingent upon the wealth being actively managed or cultivated ('amila bihi'), reflecting the Shia principle that Zakat is tied to productive growth rather than mere possession. This distinction highlights the juristic view that mental incapacity does not exempt one from Zakat if their assets are effectively utilized by guardians or stewards, a nuance critical in Shia fiqh regarding the financial responsibilities of those lacking full legal capacity.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abdul Rahman Bin Al Hajjaj who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullahasws, ‘A woman of our family is mixed up (confused - Not of right mind), ‘Is there Zakāt upon her?’ So heasws said: ‘if it was worked with, so upon her would be the Zakāt, but if it is no worked with, so no’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il has narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from ibn abu ‘Umayr from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of one of our women who is mixed (with insanity) if she is required to pay Zakat. He (the Imam) said, ‘If her assets are made to work, then Zakat is obligatory on her, but if it is not made to work, Zakat is not obligatory.’”
